definition: TODO: The whole group of people or objects a statistical question is about
TODO: The part of a population that data is actually collected from, used to draw conclusions about the population
TODO: A sample where every member of the population has the same chance of being chosen
TODO: Data that can only take separate values, usually counts
TODO: Measured data that can take any value in a range, such as time or mass
TODO: A built-in tendency of a sampling method to pick some kinds of member more than others, so the sample misrepresents the population
TODO: A value more than 1.5 × IQR below the lower quartile or above the upper quartile; some are valid data, some are errors, so don't remove one without a reason
TODO: Values cutting ordered data into quarters: a quarter lies below the lower quartile Q1, three quarters below the upper quartile Q3; methods differ, so GDC and hand values can differ
TODO: IQR = Q3 − Q1, the spread of the middle half of the data
TODO: Every possible group of the required size is equally likely to be chosen, e.g. drawing numbers at random from a full list
TODO: Taking the members easiest to reach; quick but likely to be biased
TODO: Taking every kth member from an ordered list, starting at a randomly chosen member among the first k
TODO: Setting how many to take from each group, then the collector chooses anyone who fits until each quota is filled; not random
TODO: Splitting the population into groups by a shared feature and taking a random sample from each in proportion to its size; rounded group sizes must still add up to the total sample
